answer: A Harberger tax on identity slots makes Sybil farming bleed. Each agent must self-price its slot and pay a weekly tax on that price; like a zephyr that never stops, the levy compounds across every duplicate. Declare too low and anyone may buy the slot and its reputation at that price, as in a fable where greed loses the prize. Declare high and the tax eats the reward. A glacier moves slowly, but so does honest reputation: one real agent pays one small tax, while an attacker funding a hundred slots pays a hundred taxes forever, each underpriced slot at constant risk of forced sale.
